THE PROJECT

ImageLab is a block based image processing tool. You snap Blockly blocks together into a pipeline and watch OpenCV run it on your image, which makes computer vision easy to learn.

React, Vite and TypeScript on the front end. FastAPI and PostgreSQL on the back end.

30+
Pull requests: features, bug fixes and tests
GSOC 2026
Proposal: Interactive Learning Mode
WHAT I PROPOSED

Login with JWT, saved pipelines, batch processing and step by step previews, so a learner can see what each block does to their image.

HOW I CONTRIBUTE
01
SMALL PRS
Every change gets its own branch from main and its own small pull request, so a reviewer can read it in minutes.
02
LINT FIRST
Ruff on the Python side, ESLint and Prettier on the TypeScript side, before every single commit.
03
REVIEW LOOP
When a reviewer flags something, I change exactly that and nothing else, then push the fix.
04
REAL TESTS
My tests use images with real variation. A flat colour image can pass a broken filter, so I test with images that visibly change.

QUEST 01COMPLETEUNIVERSITY PLATFORM / 2024

UNIHUB

Found 50+ student clubs with no central website, then led a team of 5 to build one platform for events, clubs and budgets.

CLASS
Team lead, full-stack
PARTY
Team of 5
WHERE
University of Birmingham Dubai
GEAR
React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Nginx, GitHub Actions, Azure
► BRIEFING

THE PROBLEM

The campus had more than 50 student clubs and no central website. Students had no single place to find events, follow clubs or see committee openings.

PROBLEM BOSS50+ CLUBS
50+ clubs, 0 central platforms. Defeated by one shared site.
50+
Student clubs with no central site
5
People on the team I led
25+
API endpoints behind the platform
► THE BIG IDEA
SHIVANI
What if students and club committees shared one platform, each with their own view?
Students browse and register for events, follow clubs and get real-time notifications. Committee members get dashboards for event engagement, job openings and the club budget.
► BATTLE LOG

THE PROCESS

ROUND 1: FIND THE GAP
Identified a campus-wide gap: 50+ clubs and no central website.
ROUND 2: BUILD
Event registration, club following, notifications, job postings and a budget tracker.
ROUND 3: SHIP
25+ API endpoints, deployed on an Azure VM behind Nginx with automated CI/CD.
► CHOICES

THREE DECISIONS THAT MATTERED

►
One platform, two audiences
Students get event registration and club discovery. Committee members get dedicated dashboards for engagement, job openings and finances.
►
Real-time notifications
Students follow clubs and get notified, so events find them instead of the other way round.
►
Production-grade delivery
Deployed on an Azure VM behind an Nginx reverse proxy, with a GitHub Actions pipeline for continuous testing and deployment.
► FINAL BUILD

A student and committee platform built with React, Node.js and PostgreSQL. Students register for events and follow clubs. Committees track engagement, post jobs and manage budgets.
